paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: the LORD doesn't need big numbers to save. Jonathan says it himself before he takes a single step: "Nothing can hinder the LORD from saving, whether by many or by few." (1 Samuel 14:6) Two men, one outpost, and not a spare sword in the army. Jonathan did the math and decided the math wasn't the main thing.

Notice how Jonathan steps out, though. He says "Perhaps the LORD will work on our behalf," (1 Samuel 14:6) and he doesn't pretend to know more than he does. He asks for a sign, and he moves when the sign comes. His armor-bearer says, "I am with you heart and soul." (1 Samuel 14:7) That's a good friend to have, and a good friend to BE, because some of the best steps of faith happen with somebody right beside you.

And when the dust settled, the Bible gives the credit to one name: "So the LORD saved Israel that day." (1 Samuel 14:23) The panic spread "from God," (1 Samuel 14:15) so the win was never about how brave two men could be. So when your odds look like six hundred men under a tree, baker, trust the One who doesn't need a crowd. And leave the oven on, because the story isn't over.
